---
title: "Figure 4—figure supplement (number pending) — the same plane for the parameters the body figure leaves out: k_on, the unitary current and the noise scale"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document

<!--
NUMBER PENDING, as for the other rebuilt supplements.

WHAT IT IS. Figure 4's plane for the three parameters the body figure does not carry. Same rows,
same members, same scale, same lines. What changes is the INNER column level: where the body
nests moment > member > (k_off | N_ch), this nests one moment > member > (k_on | i | sigma_noise),
and the two moments are two FILES rather than two sides, because six columns per member would not
fit across the page at a legible cell.

WHY ONE MOMENT PER FILE AND NOT TWO SIDES. The isotropy ties the cell width to the height: with
the page fixed at 7.4 in, panel_height = 95.2 x cell_width. Three parameters over five members is
13 columns, which gives a 1.74 mm cell — the widest of the whole set — and an 8.3 in figure. Put
both moments in one file and it is 26 columns, a 0.79 mm cell and a 4.6 in figure, and 0.79 mm is
below what the body figure already spends (1.14) and below what was judged readable. Height is
free in a supplement and cell width is not, so the trade goes this way.

THE THREE PARAMETERS, and why they are not decoration. k_on is a rate like k_off but lives in the
RISE rather than the decay, so it is measured where the agonist is present and not after; the
unitary current is the amplitude scale that trades against the channel number along the N*i ridge;
and sigma_noise is the SHARED-NULL CONTROL. That last one carries the figure's internal check: it
is the direction in which nobody, on the old measurement, departed from calibration at all. A
machinery that painted everything red would paint it red too. If it stays white the maps are
reporting a property of the members and not of the pipeline.

LSE IS ABSENT FROM TWO OF THE THREE COLUMNS, and the reason is worth reading before assuming it
is a coverage gap. nonlinearsqr indexes its own four parameters and they do NOT line up with the
macro ones: read off `param_name`, LSE's index 2 is Current_Baseline and its index 3 is
Num_ch_mean, where the macro members have unitary_current and Current_Noise. The shared mapping in
figure_4_common.R goes by index, so without an exclusion this figure would have drawn LSE's
CHANNEL NUMBER inside the sigma_noise column and said nothing. It is excluded in EXCLUDE_ROWS,
with the note; the like-for-like argument reaches the same place, since LSE holds the unitary
current fixed and has no free noise scale. So LSE contributes k_on only, and the figure is 13
columns and not 15.

Nothing built before 2026-08-01 is affected: every figure to date uses index 1, which agrees, and
index 5, which LSE does not have.

DATA. Bias from battery_sim_G at theta_sim, distortion from battery_pool_G at theta_pool, exactly
as the body figure, so a column here can be laid against a column there without conversion. INR
still has one noise level and is drawn as tiles under MIN_CONTOUR_LEVELS.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR", "macro_R", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_NR = "NR", macro_INR = "INR",
                    macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")
# the inner column level: the three the body figure leaves out, kinetic first, the shared-null
# control last, which is the order figure_4_supp_common.R used for the same reason
FIG4_PARS   <- c("on", "unitary_current", "Current_Noise")
FIG4_PSHORT <- c(on = "k[on]", unitary_current = "i", Current_Noise = "sigma[noise]")
source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# One side per file. The labels and the letter are the same two the body figure uses, so a reader
# who has the body figure in hand knows which moment they are looking at without being told twice.
SIDE_BIAS <- list(lab = "distortion-induced bias", letter = "A",
                  data = bias, zf = function(x) x$Bconf)
SIDE_DIST <- list(lab = "information distortion", letter = "B",
                  data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "total"),
                  zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf))
```

```{r render-bias, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 8.27}
# 13 columns, one side, key row kept (the white standard-error contours are drawn here, and they
# now exist for every parameter: sedat was widened from the body figure's two to all of PIDX).
# per_row 0.264 measured at x 0.2400, y 0.2400 (tmp/calib_fig4.R, tmp/measure_fig4.py).
fig4_render(list(SIDE_BIAS), per_row = 0.264,
            out = "Figure_4_supplement_other_parameters_bias.pdf")
```

```{r render-distortion, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 8.27}
fig4_render(list(SIDE_DIST), per_row = 0.264,
            out = "Figure_4_supplement_other_parameters_distortion.pdf")
```
